1 --- 2 title: Migrating to Cache Components 3 nav_title: Migrating to Cache Components 4 description: Learn how to migrate from route segment configs to Cache Components in Next.js. 5 related: 6 title: Next Steps 7 description: Learn about other behavior changes when Cache Components is enabled. 8 links: 9 - app/guides/optimizing-the-static-shell 10 - app/guides/instant-navigation 11 - app/guides/preserving-ui-state 12 - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components 13 - app/getting-started/caching 14 --- 15 16 When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). 17 18 The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight. 19 20 ## Use the adoption skill (recommended) 21 22 The [`next-cache-components-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-cache-components-adoption) skill drives this migration with a coding agent, one feature at a time, checking in at every feature boundary. It supports two modes: 23 24 - **Incremental.** Opens a single mechanical PR that opts every route out of validation, then ships each feature as a follow-up PR. This automates the [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) flow below. 25 - **Direct.** Adopts every route in place on one branch. 26 27 Install the skill: 28 29 ```bash filename="Terminal" 30 npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-adoption 31 ``` 32 33 Then give the agent this prompt: 34 35 ```prompt 36 Adopt Cache Components in this project using the next-cache-components-adoption skill. 37 ``` 38 39 ## Or migrate by hand 40 41 Migrating an existing app by hand follows a few steps, in order: 42 43 1. [Enable Cache Components](#enable-cache-components) in `next.config.ts`. 44 2. Decide your approach: convert every route now, or [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) by [opting routes out of validation](#opting-out-of-validation) first and converting one at a time. 45 3. [Follow the validation errors and insights](#following-validation) it surfaces, replacing each route segment config with its Cache Components equivalent and caching uncached data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrapping runtime data in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). The per-key sections below cover each config and API. 46 47 Your existing `fetch` and `unstable_cache` caching keeps working. Migrating `unstable_cache` is optional and can happen later. 48 49 Some surfaces have their own steps: 50 51 - For routes with dynamic params, follow the [`generateStaticParams`](#generatestaticparams-and-dynamicparams) guidance. 52 - For metadata, follow the [`generateMetadata` and `generateViewport`](#generatemetadata-and-generateviewport) guidance. 53 54 The sections below cover each config and API and what to do with it under Cache Components. 55 56 ## Enable Cache Components 57 58 Cache Components requires Next.js 16. If you're on Next.js 15 or earlier, upgrade first by following the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16). Coming from an older version, work through the [upgrade guides](/docs/app/guides/upgrading) to reach 16 before continuing. 59 60 Then enable the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) flag in `next.config.ts`: 61 62 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 63 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 64 65 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 66 cacheComponents: true, 67 } 68 69 export default nextConfig 70 ``` 71 72 > **Good to know:** If you were using `experimental.dynamicIO` or `experimental.useCache`, `cacheComponents` replaces them. See the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). 73 74 After enabling the flag, route segments that still export `dynamic`, `revalidate`, or `fetchCache` will error. Start by replacing those configs. The sections below explain what to do for each one. 75 76 ## Opting out of validation 77 78 A validation insight or error tells you a route won't render instantly. Resolve it by following the recommendation: cache the data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrap it in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). If you're not ready to address it yet, set the [`instant`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) config to `false` on the segment that raised it (a layout, page, or parallel slot), then come back to it later. 79 80 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" 81 export const instant = false 82 ``` 83 84 > **Good to know**: `instant = false` marks a segment as _allowed to block_. It does not force the route to be dynamic, so a genuinely prerenderable route still ships a static shell. It also does not clear synchronous IO build errors: calls like `new Date()`, `Math.random()`, and `crypto.randomUUID()` still fail the prerender. See [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally). 85 86 ## Adopting incrementally 87 88 You don't have to migrate every route at once. `instant = false` lets you get the whole app building and running first, then convert routes one at a time: 89 90 1. **Enable the flag and migrate each route segment config.** Follow the relevant sections below for [`dynamic = "force-dynamic"`](#dynamic--force-dynamic), [`dynamic = "force-static"`](#dynamic--force-static), [`dynamic = "error"`](#dynamic--error), [`revalidate`](#revalidate), and [`fetchCache`](#fetchcache). For routes with dynamic params, also follow the [`generateStaticParams`](#generatestaticparams-and-dynamicparams) guidance. Routes that still render instantly need no further work. 91 2. **Opt out the routes that aren't ready.** Where an insight or error appears, set `instant = false` on the segment that raised it. To do this in one pass across the whole app, run the [`cache-components-instant-false`](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#cache-components-instant-false) codemod, which adds the opt-out to every `page`, `layout`, and `default` that doesn't already declare `instant`: 92 93 ```bash filename="Terminal" 94 npx @next/codemod@canary cache-components-instant-false ./app 95 ``` 96 97 > **Good to know**: Pass `./src/app` in a `src/` project. A wrong path reports `0 ok` instead of failing, so check the file count. 98 99 The app keeps building and serving, now with validation deferred for the opted-out routes. 100 101 3. **Fix synchronous IO. It can't be deferred.** Calls like `new Date()`, `Date.now()`, `Math.random()`, and `crypto.randomUUID()` during prerender throw a build error that `instant = false` does not clear, so a route that uses them won't build until you address it, opt-out or not. Move the call out of the prerendered shell so it runs at request time: wrap the part that needs it in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) and call [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) before the call, or move it into a Client Component. 102 4. **Convert one route at a time.** Remove `instant = false` from a route, then resolve its insights by caching data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrapping runtime data in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). Repeat until no routes opt out. 103 104 ## Following validation 105 106 Cache Components validates your routes in development and surfaces errors and insights in the dev overlay. Some look like this, naming the affected component and pointing at a fix: 107 108 109 ' }, 117 { text: '}' }, 118 ]} 119 /> 120 ', highlight: true }, 126 { text: ' ' }, 127 { text: '', highlight: true }, 128 ]} 129 /> 130 131 132 Each card is clickable and opens a page with patterns, code samples, and trade-offs. Work through the insights and errors until they're gone. For the full validation workflow, the DevTools, and CI testing, see the [instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation). 133 134 Insights don't show up in the HTTP response. An offending route still returns `200` with rendered HTML in dev. The insight only appears in the dev overlay, the dev-server log, or the [MCP `get_errors` tool](/docs/app/guides/mcp). To see them, read the overlay (or query the MCP). 135 136 ## `dynamic = "force-dynamic"` 137 138 **Remove the config.** Without Cache Components, `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` rendered the entire route for every request and made its `fetch` requests uncached. With Cache Components, uncached data and [Request-time APIs](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) already run at request time. Next.js prerenders any static or cached UI around them. 139 140 After removing the config, [follow any validation errors or insights](#following-validation) that appear. 141 142 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 143 // Before 144 export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' 145 146 export default function Page() { 147 return
...
148 } 149 ``` 150 151 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 152 // Before 153 export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' 154 155 export default function Page() { 156 return
...
157 } 158 ``` 159 160 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 161 // After 162 export default function Page() { 163 return
...
164 } 165 ``` 166 167 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 168 // After 169 export default function Page() { 170 return
...
171 } 172 ``` 173 174 ## `dynamic = "force-static"` 175 176 **Remove the config, then make its caching explicit.** Without Cache Components, `dynamic = 'force-static'` forced the route to prerender, cached its data, and made `cookies()`, `headers()`, and `useSearchParams()` return empty values. 177 178 Cache data that should be reused with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and a suitable [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). After removing the config, Request-time APIs read actual request values. Remove those dependencies if the route must remain fully prerendered. 179 180 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 181 // Before 182 export const dynamic = 'force-static' 183 184 export default async function Page() { 185 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 186 return
...
187 } 188 ``` 189 190 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 191 // Before 192 export const dynamic = 'force-static' 193 194 export default async function Page() { 195 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 196 return
...
197 } 198 ``` 199 200 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 201 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 202 203 // After 204 export default async function Page() { 205 'use cache' 206 cacheLife('max') 207 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 208 return
...
209 } 210 ``` 211 212 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 213 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 214 215 // After 216 export default async function Page() { 217 'use cache' 218 cacheLife('max') 219 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 220 return
...
221 } 222 ``` 223 224 ### Enforce static output 225 226 > **Good to know**: `ensureStatic` is available in Next.js 16.4 and later. This step is optional. Add it only if the route still has a static output requirement after the migration. 227 228 To require a completely static route, add [`ensureStatic = 'navigation'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic#navigation) after migrating its caching: 229 230 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 231 export const ensureStatic = 'navigation' 232 ``` 233 234 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 235 export const ensureStatic = 'navigation' 236 ``` 237 238 Unlike `dynamic = 'force-static'`, `ensureStatic` does not make Request-time APIs return empty values. It reports an error if request-specific server work prevents the route from being prerendered. If only the App Shell or per-link prefetch must stay static, choose a less restrictive level. See [Keeping pages static](/docs/app/guides/keeping-pages-static). 239 240 ## `dynamic = "error"` 241 242 **Remove the config.** Without Cache Components, `dynamic = 'error'` required the route to prerender and treated `fetch` requests as cached by default. It raised an error only when uncached data or a Request-time API prevented prerendering. 243 244 After removing the config, `fetch` no longer inherits that cached default. To preserve the route's existing caching behavior, wrap those requests in [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and set their lifetime with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). If the route did not rely on the default, no replacement is needed. 245 246 ### Enforce static validation 247 248 > **Good to know**: `ensureStatic` is available in Next.js 16.4 and later. This step is optional. Add it only if the route still has a static output requirement after the migration. 249 250 To require a completely static route, add [`ensureStatic = 'navigation'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic#navigation) after making the route's caching explicit: 251 252 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 253 export const ensureStatic = 'navigation' 254 ``` 255 256 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 257 export const ensureStatic = 'navigation' 258 ``` 259 260 Use a less restrictive level when only the App Shell or per-link prefetch must stay static. See [Keeping pages static](/docs/app/guides/keeping-pages-static) for how to choose a level. 261 262 ## `revalidate` 263 264 **Replace revalidation times greater than zero with `cacheLife`.** Without Cache Components, `revalidate` set the default revalidation time for an entire route. With Cache Components, place [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) around the data or UI that should be cached, then set its lifetime with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). 265 266 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 267 // Before 268 export const revalidate = 3600 // 1 hour 269 270 export default async function Page() { 271 return
...
272 } 273 ``` 274 275 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 276 // Before 277 export const revalidate = 3600 // 1 hour 278 279 export default async function Page() { 280 return
...
281 } 282 ``` 283 284 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 285 // After 286 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 287 288 export default async function Page() { 289 'use cache' 290 cacheLife('hours') 291 return
...
292 } 293 ``` 294 295 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 296 // After 297 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 298 299 export default async function Page() { 300 'use cache' 301 cacheLife('hours') 302 return
...
303 } 304 ``` 305 306 > **Good to know**: If your `revalidate` value doesn't match a built-in [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) profile (`'seconds'`, `'minutes'`, `'hours'`, `'days'`, `'weeks'`, `'max'`), pick the closest one or define a [custom profile](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#custom-cache-profiles) to match your conventions. You can also [redefine a built-in profile](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#overriding-the-default-cache-profiles), including `default`, when its timings don't match your application's caching needs. 307 308 For `revalidate = 0`, remove the config. Uncached data already runs at request time with Cache Components. Keep data outside a `use cache` scope when it must run for every request. 309 310 ## `fetchCache` 311 312 **Remove the config and set caching at the data source.** Without Cache Components, `fetchCache` changed or restricted the `cache` option for every `fetch` request in a route. With Cache Components, fetches are uncached unless they run inside a `use cache` scope. 313 314 For `default-cache`, `only-cache`, or `force-cache`, wrap the data that should remain cached in [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache). For `default-no-store`, `only-no-store`, or `force-no-store`, leave the data outside a cache scope. If `force-no-store` previously overrode an explicit cache option, remove that option as well. 315 316 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 317 // Before 318 export const fetchCache = 'force-cache' 319 ``` 320 321 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 322 // Before 323 export const fetchCache = 'force-cache' 324 ``` 325 326 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 327 // After 328 export default async function Page() { 329 'use cache' 330 // All fetches here are cached 331 return
...
332 } 333 ``` 334 335 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 336 // After 337 export default async function Page() { 338 'use cache' 339 // All fetches here are cached 340 return
...
341 } 342 ``` 343 344 ## `fetch` cache options 345 346 **Move `cache` and `next` options to `use cache`.** 347 348 Without Cache Components, you cache a request with `cache: 'force-cache'` and tune it with `next: { revalidate, tags }`. 349 350 With Cache Components, wrap the fetch in a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) function. Fetches inside that scope are cached automatically, and `revalidate` and `tags` become [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag). 351 352 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 353 // Before 354 export default async function Page() { 355 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data', { 356 cache: 'force-cache', 357 next: { revalidate: 3600, tags: ['data'] }, 358 }) 359 const data = await res.json() 360 return
...
361 } 362 ``` 363 364 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 365 // Before 366 export default async function Page() { 367 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data', { 368 cache: 'force-cache', 369 next: { revalidate: 3600, tags: ['data'] }, 370 }) 371 const data = await res.json() 372 return
...
373 } 374 ``` 375 376 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 377 // After 378 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 379 380 async function getData() { 381 'use cache' 382 cacheLife('hours') 383 cacheTag('data') 384 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 385 return res.json() 386 } 387 388 export default async function Page() { 389 const data = await getData() 390 return
...
391 } 392 ``` 393 394 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 395 // After 396 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 397 398 async function getData() { 399 'use cache' 400 cacheLife('hours') 401 cacheTag('data') 402 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 403 return res.json() 404 } 405 406 export default async function Page() { 407 const data = await getData() 408 return
...
409 } 410 ``` 411 412 Note the persistence difference. The `fetch` Data Cache persists cached responses across deployments and across serverless instances. 413 414 `use cache` defaults to in-memory storage, so its entries are discarded when the serverless instance is destroyed and are scoped to a single deployment. Use [`use cache: remote`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) or a [cache handler](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers) for storage that survives instance teardown. Even with durable storage, expect cached values to recompute after a new deployment. 415 416 ## `unstable_cache` 417 418 **No change required.** 419 420 `unstable_cache` continues to work with Cache Components. You can leave it in place and migrate it later. 421 422 If you choose to migrate it, turn the wrapped function into a function with the `'use cache'` directive. The cache key is derived automatically from the arguments, so the key-parts array is no longer needed, and the `options` object maps to [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag). 423 424 ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher 425 // Before 426 import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache' 427 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 428 429 export const getUser = unstable_cache( 430 async (id: string) => { 431 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 432 }, 433 ['user'], // cache key prefix 434 { tags: ['users'], revalidate: 3600 } 435 ) 436 ``` 437 438 ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher 439 // Before 440 import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache' 441 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 442 443 export const getUser = unstable_cache( 444 async (id) => { 445 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 446 }, 447 ['user'], // cache key prefix 448 { tags: ['users'], revalidate: 3600 } 449 ) 450 ``` 451 452 ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher 453 // After 454 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 455 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 456 457 export async function getUser(id: string) { 458 'use cache' 459 cacheLife('hours') 460 cacheTag('users') 461 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 462 } 463 ``` 464 465 ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher 466 // After 467 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 468 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 469 470 export async function getUser(id) { 471 'use cache' 472 cacheLife('hours') 473 cacheTag('users') 474 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 475 } 476 ``` 477 478 Like the `fetch` Data Cache, `unstable_cache` persists cached values across deployments and serverless instances, while `use cache` does not. See [`fetch` cache options](#fetch-cache-options) above for the storage details. 479 480 ## `React.cache` 481 482 **Usually no change.** `React.cache` continues to deduplicate matching calls within a React render. 483 484 However, each Cache Function has an isolated React cache scope. Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.

> **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.

## Use the adoption skill (recommended)

The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.

Install the skill:

```bash filename="Terminal"
npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
```

Then give the agent this prompt:

```prompt
Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
```

## Or adopt by hand

To adopt an existing app by hand:

1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.

Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.

```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
import type { NextConfig } from 'next'

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
  partialPrefetching: true,
}

export default nextConfig
```

A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |

| `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |

The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
